jobs.description:
Senior Client Relations Specialist

Are you an experienced client relations or account management professional who knows how to build strong relationships, resolve challenges, and identify opportunities for account growth?

Join KALAM as a Senior Client Relations Specialist and take ownership of a portfolio of clients, acting as the primary link between them and our internal teams. You will play a key role in strengthening client satisfaction, supporting retention and renewals, managing escalations, and identifying opportunities to expand our partnerships.

About the Role

As a Senior Client Relations Specialist, you will manage the day-to-day relationship with assigned clients and develop a strong understanding of their business, priorities, expectations, and evolving needs.

This role goes beyond responding to client requests. You will proactively monitor account health, identify potential risks, coordinate the resolution of service issues, support renewals, and uncover opportunities for account growth.

You will work closely with Operations, Service Delivery, Quality, Finance, Business Development, Technology, and other internal teams to ensure client commitments are clearly communicated and effectively delivered.

Key Responsibilities

Client Relationship & Portfolio Management

  • Own the day-to-day relationship for an assigned portfolio of clients.
  • Act as the primary coordination point between clients and KALAM's internal teams.
  • Develop a deep understanding of each client's business, operating model, requirements, priorities, and contractual commitments.
  • Build trusted professional relationships with stakeholders at different organizational levels.
  • Maintain proactive and regular communication with clients.
  • Ensure clients receive accurate, professional, consistent, and timely communication.
  • Monitor overall account health and proactively identify potential risks and opportunities.

Client Experience & Retention

  • Monitor client satisfaction and the overall client experience across assigned accounts.
  • Identify early signs of dissatisfaction, service concerns, relationship deterioration, or potential churn.
  • Coordinate proactive actions with internal teams before issues escalate.
  • Support client retention and renewal activities.
  • Gather, document, and communicate client feedback to relevant stakeholders.
  • Help strengthen relationships that position KALAM as a trusted long-term business partner.

Complaint & Escalation Management

  • Own client complaints and escalations from acknowledgment through resolution and closure.
  • Assess issue urgency, severity, and business impact.
  • Coordinate with Operations, Service Delivery, Quality, Finance, Technology, and other relevant teams to resolve issues.
  • Keep clients informed throughout the resolution process.
  • Follow up on agreed actions and ensure commitments are completed.
  • Support root-cause analysis to help prevent recurring issues.
  • Escalate major relationship, service, contractual, or financial risks when required.

Account Growth & Commercial Opportunities

  • Identify potential opportunities for account expansion, upselling, cross-selling, and additional services.
  • Understand changing client requirements and translate them into potential business opportunities.
  • Qualify potential opportunities before escalating them to the Senior Client Relations Manager and/or Business Development team.
  • Provide relevant client and account intelligence to support opportunity development.
  • Coordinate internally to confirm operational feasibility before commitments are made.
  • Support proposals, renewals, and account expansion discussions.
  • Maintain ownership of the overall client relationship while senior management or Business Development leads final commercial negotiations.

Renewals & Contract Support

  • Monitor upcoming contract renewals and begin preparations well in advance.
  • Review client satisfaction, account performance, risks, outstanding issues, and potential growth opportunities before renewal discussions.
  • Coordinate required information with internal stakeholders.
  • Support renewal negotiations and discussions.
  • Ensure agreed contractual changes and client commitments are clearly communicated internally.

Financial & Collection Support

  • Maintain awareness of the financial status of assigned client accounts.
  • Coordinate with Finance regarding overdue invoices and collection priorities.
  • Follow up professionally with clients regarding outstanding balances.
  • Escalate payment disputes, recurring collection issues, or financial risks when needed.
  • Coordinate with Finance to resolve client queries related to invoices.

Client Intelligence & Forecasting

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date information on assigned accounts.
  • Track changes in client demand, expected volumes, service requirements, business conditions, and expansion plans.
  • Share relevant client insights with Operations, Planning & Control, Finance, Business Development, and other stakeholders.
  • Support operational and commercial forecasting through timely client intelligence.
  • Identify relevant market or competitor information obtained through client interactions.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Collaborate closely with Service Delivery, Operations, Planning & Control, Quality, Finance, Business Development, Technology, and other departments.
  • Translate client requirements into clear and actionable internal information.
  • Ensure internal stakeholders understand client priorities and commitments.
  • Coordinate cross-functional actions related to assigned accounts.
  • Follow up on delays, gaps, conflicting information, or unresolved actions that may affect the client relationship.
  • Ensure external commitments remain aligned with KALAM's operational capabilities.

Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management, Marketing, Communications, or a related field.

Experience

  • 3–4 years of relevant professional experience.
  • At least 2–3 years of experience in Client Relations, Account Management, Customer Success, Service Delivery, BPO, or a similar client-facing role.
  • Proven experience managing multiple client accounts or stakeholder relationships simultaneously.
  • Previous experience within BPO, outsourcing, interpretation, contact centers, customer experience, or professional services is highly preferred.

Key Competencies

  • Client Relationship Management
  • Account Management
  • Customer Success & Retention
  • Complaint & Escalation Management
  • Stakeholder Management
  • Cross-Functional Coordination
  • Business Development & Account Growth
  • Negotiation & Commercial Awareness
  • Problem Solving
  • Communication & Presentation Skills
  • Client Reporting & Account Intelligence
  • Time Management & Prioritization

Why Join KALAM?

KALAM provides language and business-process solutions to organizations across international markets, with services covering areas such as remote interpretation, customer experience management, shared services, and digital CX.

If you are passionate about building strong client partnerships, solving complex challenges, and contributing to long-term account growth, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
About the role

Comms8 is looking for a hands-on Bookkeeper & Finance Admin to take ownership of our day-to-day bookkeeping and finance administration across our group.

This is a practical, detail-focused role for someone who is comfortable keeping financial records accurate and up to date, reconciling accounts, processing invoices and expenses, and preparing regular finance reports.

You will support four entities across two jurisdictions and work closely with our team and accountants in the UK and Hong Kong.

Importantly, our UK and Hong Kong accountants handle all statutory filings and audit requirements. You will provide accurate records and information to support them, but you will not be responsible for owning statutory compliance or audit.

The role will initially focus entirely on finance. Once the month-end process is running accurately and consistently, the role will gradually expand to include general administrative support.

What you'll be doing

Finance & Bookkeeping

  • Manage day-to-day bookkeeping across four group entities
  • Complete regular bank reconciliations and investigate discrepancies
  • Manage accounts payable and accounts receivable
  • Prepare and issue client invoices and follow up on outstanding payments
  • Process and record business expenses
  • Prepare payroll data for UK employees and offshore contractors
  • Record and reconcile intercompany transactions between business entities
  • Produce a standard monthly finance pack
  • Prepare a weekly cash and aged-debtors report using an established template
  • Maintain accurate and well-organised financial records
  • Respond to queries and provide supporting information to our UK and Hong Kong accountants
  • Support month-end processes and help ensure the books are complete, accurate and ready for accountant review

You will not be expected to handle statutory filings or audits as these will be managed by our UK and Hong Kong accountants, giving you the opportunity to focus on maintaining accurate books and running the day-to-day finance processes well.

Admin Support

Once you have established a reliable month-end routine, the role will expand to include:

  • Contractor onboarding and offboarding paperwork
  • Vendor, subscription and business-tool administration
  • Document filing and record-keeping across the four entities
  • General administrative support for the operations team

What we're looking for

  • 2–5 years of experience in bookkeeping, finance administration or a similar hands-on finance role
  • Solid experience with day-to-day bookkeeping and bank reconciliations
  • Experience handling accounts payable, accounts receivable, invoicing and expenses
  • Good understanding of month-end bookkeeping processes
  • Strong numerical accuracy and attention to detail
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment
  • Organised and consistent in maintaining records and following established processes
  • Confident communicating with colleagues and accountants
  • Good written and spoken English
  • Comfortable working across multiple entities and currencies
  • Able to work the required hours with regular overlap with our UK and Hong Kong teams

Experience preparing payroll data, handling intercompany transactions or working with international/remote businesses would be an advantage.

Working arrangement

This is a full-time contractor engagement, not an employment position.

The role is fully remote and open to candidates based across Southeast Asia.

Because you will work closely with colleagues and accountants across the UK and Hong Kong, availability during the required working hours and sufficient overlap with both teams is a mandatory requirement for this role.

Compensation

USD 500–800 per month, depending on relevant experience and demonstrated bookkeeping capability.

What success looks like

In your first few months, the priority will be straightforward: accurate books, clean reconciliations and a dependable month-end process.

Once the finance routine is running smoothly, you will begin supporting selected administrative tasks across the business.

If you are a practical, organised bookkeeper who enjoys keeping financial records accurate and processes running consistently, we'd be pleased to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Position Available

The Food Research & Action Center (FRAC) seeks a talented and experienced Senior Policy Analyst to join its Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) team. This position offers an opportunity to help shape national and state policy at a critical moment for SNAP and to be part of a collaborative team working to protect, restore, and strengthen food assistance for individuals and families across the country.

The Senior Policy Analyst will analyze federal and state SNAP policy, translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into actionable information, and support advocacy strategies designed to protect access to benefits and strengthen program administration. The ideal candidate brings strong policy analysis and writing skills, substantive experience with SNAP, and the ability to move effectively between detailed policy analysis and broader advocacy strategy.

This is a fully remote position that offers opportunities to work in coalition with FRAC’s national, state, and local partners and to expand experience as a program analyst, strategist, coalition builder, and project manager. This position works closely with the SNAP Director and other Senior SNAP Policy Analyst. While this role is primarily remote, significant priority will be given to candidates based in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, including nearby Northern Virginia and Maryland suburbs.

Organizational Background

FRAC works to improve the nutrition, health, and well-being of people struggling against poverty-related hunger in the United States through advocacy, partnerships, and by advancing bold and equitable policy solutions. To attain this mission, FRAC engages in research, policy analysis and advocacy, coalition-building, outreach, technical assistance and training, and an array of communications strategies. In partnership with hundreds of national, state, and local nonprofit organizations, public agencies, corporations, and labor organizations, FRAC addresses hunger and food insecurity, and poverty as their root cause.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Analyze SNAP data and research to identify trends, disparities, implementation challenges, and opportunities to improve program access.
  • Evaluate the effects of existing or proposed legislation, regulations, policies and practices to determine ways and provide guidance to defend, improve and expand SNAP’s positive impacts.
  • Make recommendations for policy changes to streamline, improve accessibility, and increase SNAP compliance.
  • Write and/or assist with persuasive analytic and research materials, guides, outreach materials, and reports for use by advocates, government agencies, policy makers, service providers, and the media.
  • Make presentations to diverse audiences at local, state, regional and national conferences and meetings on SNAP access, benefit adequacy, and quality customer service.

  • Provide information, technical assistance, analysis, training, strategic advice, and other hands-on support to national, state and community-based organizations, state and local government agencies, private nonprofit organizations, and activists regarding ways to strengthen SNAP’s access, benefit adequacy, reach, and quality customer service.
  • Provide expertise and support to other program areas and departments assigned by the SNAP Director.
  • Represent FRAC at coalition and partner meetings.
  • Assist in managing regrants to national, state, and local nonprofits and provide technical assistance to the regrantees.
  • Other performance tasks as assigned.

Skills and Experience

The ideal candidate will possess the following characteristics:

  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in advocacy, program operations, policy analysis and/or organizing.
  • Advanced degree in public policy, law, public administration, social work, economics, public health, or related discipline required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of SNAP.
  • Strong policy research, analysis, and writing skills, including the ability to interpret complex statutes, regulations, and administrative guidance.
  • Ability to evaluate policies, processes, or programs to identify issues and recommend solutions.
  • Ability to communicate technical policy issues clearly to both specialized and nontechnical audiences.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Experience in nonprofit, government or policy work strongly preferred.
  • Ability to tap input and engagement from people with lived experience with hunger and poverty strongly preferred.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.
  • Commitment to FRAC’s mission and to improving access to nutrition assistance for people with low incomes.
  • Ability to work independently and as a member of a team.

Salary/Benefits

The salary range for this position is $86,000 - $89,000 depending on qualifications and experience. Generous leave, health, retirement, and other benefits. FRAC’s normal office hours are between 9:00 am and 5:30 pm Eastern. This position is part of a union and is covered under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement.

No phone calls or emails, please.

Opening/Closing Dates

Applications close 11:59 pm ET on Friday, September 4, 2026

FRAC is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer. FRAC is firmly committed to a policy against discrimination based on age, gender, race, religious creed, sexual orientation, disability, or ethnic or national origin.

jobs.description:
About the role

Comms8 is looking for a hands-on Bookkeeper & Finance Admin to take ownership of our day-to-day bookkeeping and finance administration across our group.

This is a practical, detail-focused role for someone who is comfortable keeping financial records accurate and up to date, reconciling accounts, processing invoices and expenses, and preparing regular finance reports.

You will support four entities across two jurisdictions and work closely with our team and accountants in the UK and Hong Kong.

Importantly, our UK and Hong Kong accountants handle all statutory filings and audit requirements. You will provide accurate records and information to support them, but you will not be responsible for owning statutory compliance or audit.

The role will initially focus entirely on finance. Once the month-end process is running accurately and consistently, the role will gradually expand to include general administrative support.

What you'll be doing

Finance & Bookkeeping

  • Manage day-to-day bookkeeping across four group entities
  • Complete regular bank reconciliations and investigate discrepancies
  • Manage accounts payable and accounts receivable
  • Prepare and issue client invoices and follow up on outstanding payments
  • Process and record business expenses
  • Prepare payroll data for UK employees and offshore contractors
  • Record and reconcile intercompany transactions between business entities
  • Produce a standard monthly finance pack
  • Prepare a weekly cash and aged-debtors report using an established template
  • Maintain accurate and well-organised financial records
  • Respond to queries and provide supporting information to our UK and Hong Kong accountants
  • Support month-end processes and help ensure the books are complete, accurate and ready for accountant review

You will not be expected to handle statutory filings or audits as these will be managed by our UK and Hong Kong accountants, giving you the opportunity to focus on maintaining accurate books and running the day-to-day finance processes well.

Admin Support

Once you have established a reliable month-end routine, the role will expand to include:

  • Contractor onboarding and offboarding paperwork
  • Vendor, subscription and business-tool administration
  • Document filing and record-keeping across the four entities
  • General administrative support for the operations team

What we're looking for

  • 2–5 years of experience in bookkeeping, finance administration or a similar hands-on finance role
  • Solid experience with day-to-day bookkeeping and bank reconciliations
  • Experience handling accounts payable, accounts receivable, invoicing and expenses
  • Good understanding of month-end bookkeeping processes
  • Strong numerical accuracy and attention to detail
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment
  • Organised and consistent in maintaining records and following established processes
  • Confident communicating with colleagues and accountants
  • Good written and spoken English
  • Comfortable working across multiple entities and currencies
  • Able to work the required hours with regular overlap with our UK and Hong Kong teams

Experience preparing payroll data, handling intercompany transactions or working with international/remote businesses would be an advantage.

Working arrangement

This is a full-time contractor engagement, not an employment position.

The role is fully remote and open to candidates based across Southeast Asia.

Because you will work closely with colleagues and accountants across the UK and Hong Kong, availability during the required working hours and sufficient overlap with both teams is a mandatory requirement for this role.

Compensation

USD 500–800 per month, depending on relevant experience and demonstrated bookkeeping capability.

What success looks like

In your first few months, the priority will be straightforward: accurate books, clean reconciliations and a dependable month-end process.

Once the finance routine is running smoothly, you will begin supporting selected administrative tasks across the business.

If you are a practical, organised bookkeeper who enjoys keeping financial records accurate and processes running consistently, we'd be pleased to hear from you.

jobs.excerpt: About the jobARS Logistics (Authorized Agent of Trinity Logistics) is a family owned and operated Third Party Logistics company with 20+ years of history.
jobs.description:
About the job

ARS Logistics (Authorized Agent of Trinity Logistics) is a family owned and operated Third Party Logistics company with 20+ years of history. We are proud of what we have built through strong and lasting relationships with our customers and team members.

ARS moves freight across all modes for our customers — Truckload, LTL, Intermodal, Drayage, Ocean and Air. Our customers count on us for consistent capacity on the lanes they ship every week, not just whoever happens to be posted on a load board that morning. We are hiring a dedicated Carrier Sourcing Representative whose whole job is building that capacity: calling carriers, learning their lanes and equipment, and lining up committed trucks on our regular and hard-to-cover lanes weeks before the freight moves.

This is an outbound, phone-first role. You will own a set of target lanes, build a bench of vetted carriers on each one, and hand our operations and account teams capacity they can sell and book — so we cover on time, buy at or below market, and rely less on the spot board. Success is measured in carriers added, lanes with committed capacity, and loads covered by relationship carriers.

Start date: ASAP

Why you’ll like working here

  • A focused job — sourcing and relationships, not dispatch and paperwork.
  • Results you can see — lanes that used to be a daily scramble become routine because of the carriers you found.
  • Collaborative team — you work side by side with our operations, customer service and sales teams, who value open communication and follow-through.
  • Structured upward mobility — a clear growth path as the carrier team expands (senior sourcing, carrier team lead).

What you’ll do

  • Make high-volume outbound calls and emails to carriers, dispatchers and owner-operators to source capacity on assigned lanes — regular weekly lanes, capacity-constrained lanes, and new lanes from customer bids.
  • Build and maintain a carrier bench for every target lane: preferred lanes, equipment, trucks per week, rate expectations and contacts, kept current in our CRM / TMS.
  • Secure capacity and rate commitments weeks ahead, then hand them to operations and account managers so the capacity can be presold to customers and booked on the right dates.
  • Find capacity that never reaches a load board — asset carriers’ headhaul and backhaul lanes, small fleets with consistent routes, and dedicated or recurring-lane programs.
  • Vet every new carrier before it is offered freight: operating authority, insurance, safety record, and double-brokering or identity-fraud red flags, using our carrier onboarding and monitoring tools.
  • Collect carrier rate feedback for customer quotes and RFPs / RFQs so our pricing reflects real cost.
  • Keep relationships warm — regular check-ins, service feedback, and fast resolution of load or payment questions with our operations and accounting teams.
  • Report weekly on lanes covered, carriers added, committed capacity and cost versus market.

What you need to bring

  • 1+ year (2+ preferred) in carrier sales, capacity sourcing or carrier development at a U.S. freight brokerage / 3PL — truckload (dry van, reefer, flatbed).
  • Proven outbound phone volume: comfortable making 60+ carrier calls a day and negotiating with U.S. dispatchers and owner-operators.
  • Working knowledge of DAT and / or Truckstop load boards and rate data, and lane terminology (headhaul, backhaul, deadhead, all-in, linehaul vs. fuel).
  • Understanding of carrier compliance — MC / DOT authority, certificates of insurance, safety ratings — and common double-brokering and identity-fraud schemes.
  • Clear, confident spoken English and professional written English.
  • Disciplined record keeping: every call, carrier and commitment logged in a CRM / TMS the same day.
  • Operational in Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel.
  • Reliable remote setup: backup power, backup internet, backup computer, 2 to 3 screens, and a noise-cancelling headset.
  • Availability during core U.S. Eastern business hours (see engagement details).

Preference given to

  • Experience building dedicated or recurring-lane carrier programs.
  • Carrier onboarding / monitoring tools such as Highway, RMIS, Carrier Assure or MyCarrierPackets.
  • Dialpad or similar VoIP phone systems; Zoho or another CRM.
  • Prior experience supporting a Trinity Logistics agency or another agent-model brokerage.
  • Reefer, flatbed, drayage or cross-border (Mexico) carrier networks; Spanish.

Engagement details

  • Engagement type: Remote independent contractor, Philippines-based.
  • Core availability: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM U.S. Eastern (1-hour lunch); final schedule may be adjusted based on team coverage. Occasional after-hours carrier calls (infrequent).
  • Compensation: $940 – $1,150 USD per month, based on experience, plus a performance incentive tied to committed capacity and loads covered, with a structured growth plan.
  • Time off: 15 paid business days per calendar year after 90 days, per contract structure.
  • Reports to: Operations Manager.
  • Travel: None.

How to apply

Apply with your resume and answer the screening questions on the application. The screening questions include a link to a 60-second voice recording (Google Drive, Vocaroo or similar) of you introducing yourself to a U.S. carrier dispatcher and asking about their lanes. Applications without the recording will not be reviewed.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, sex, disability, veteran or other protected status.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Co-Impact brings together local changemakers and funders from around the world to make health, education, and economic systems stronger and more inclusive – creating impact that lasts. Our commitment to advancing gender equality and women’s leadership is central to this goal. By focusing on systems, we work at the scale of the problem - dismantling the root causes of inequality that disadvantage hundreds of millions of women, girls and marginalized communities. Spanning five continents, our team identifies partners that will create lasting progress when supported with the resources to work at scale. Pooling funding allows us to provide large, flexible grants and strategic support to locally-rooted partners in Africa, Asia, and Latin America who know their systems best. Our partners' initiatives will benefit more than 600 million people, and we can go even further together. We aim to deploy over $1 billion by 2030 and achieve a world where everyone can lead fulfilling lives. For more information, please visit and take a look at our Handbook.

Co-Impact partners with Professional Employment Organizations (PEOs) to employ their staff.

The Role

Reporting to the Vice President, Programs you will serve as a senior program leader, responsible for sourcing, vetting and finalizing grant recommendations in Asia. You will support program partners (grantees) to develop effective strategies for gender equality, women’s leadership and systems change at scale, while enhancing organizational capabilities for sustainable impact. Additionally, you will contribute to advancing learning and practice among partners, within Co-Impact, the global development sector, and philanthropy.

You bring a strong commitment to gender equality, inclusion, and justice, demonstrated through strategic acumen, an abiding curiosity, and a desire to learn. You also bring excellent interpersonal and analytical skills, along with a high level of personal initiative and the ability to thrive in a distributed, diverse, deep-thinking, and fast-paced environment. You are driven by a focus on root causes, justice, and solving social issues at the systems level and at scale.

You have 15+ years of relevant experience in gender and global development, including at least 5 years in grant-making and supporting program partners. You possess substantial experience working within and understanding the political economies of your regional context. Fluency in English is required.

Responsibilities

As the lead for the region, you will be accountable for achieving Co-Impact’s goals at both the regional and global levels. Core responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

Strategy Development and Implementation: Program Partners

Lead the regional team in developing, implementing and monitoring a contextualized Co-Impact program strategy and implementation at a portfolio level. Contribute to ongoing reflection and enhancement of Co-Impact’s strategy and programs, theory and practice of systems change, gender equality, and organizational strengthening. Support the overall model to achieve shared goals ensuring that the regional program strategy aligns with and contributes to global and cross-regional plans. This includes:

  • Annual Program partner support plan: In consultation with the regional team, the Regional Director (RD) will lead the development of annual support plans for existing program partners – categorized by their grant phase – design phase and post-design phase. The RD will conduct regular check-ins with team members to ensure that support for program partner (PP) is on track, address any issues as they arise, and monitor PP progress throughout the grant.
  • Develop external support streams for regional PPs: Working closely with cross-regional teams such as the Design Team and the LME Team, the Regional Director will identify various streams for support for PPs including coach support, communities of practice and LME support.
  • Oversee the development and implementation of scalable systems and processes to ensure sourcing and PP support are well-planned, process-driven and institutionalized.
  • Oversee the development of the regional sourcing strategy and approach document, designed to identify and engage new program partners. The RD is responsible for ensuring alignment with Co-Impacts’ overall goals, issue areas and regional priorities.
  • Regional Learning Strategy: Take responsibility for consolidating lessons and insights for the region in partnership with the LME Director. Collaborate with the LME team, fellow Directors and account teams to distil key lessons and insights from evidence and data across themes, partners and regions.
  • Serve as an account lead for select program partners (PPs) to ensuring a strong alignment with the programmatic work.
  • Communications: Serve as a spokesperson for the organization representing Co-Impact regionally and with global stakeholders, working closely with the Communications team.
  • Philanthropy: Working closely with the Philanthropy and Communications team and the Strategic Partnerships team, to cultivate relationships with key funders in the respective region.
  • Engaging champions: Provide input and ideas on engagement plans in the region for funders and Boards.
  • Play a key role in facilitating cross-learning and knowledge sharing across regions and sub-teams. Intentionally incorporate and disseminate lessons learned, particularly with other Program directors.

Management and Leadership

  • Provide strategic leadership for the region by establishing and expanding Co-Impact’s presence and cultivating partnerships in the region.
  • Cultivate and maintain trusted relationships with senior government and public sector stakeholders, as needed, helping position Co-Impact as a credible long-term partner while navigating complex political, policy, and regulatory contexts across the region.
  • Develop and oversee the regional budget on an annual basis.
  • Lead and sustain a motivated, high-performing, inclusive and diverse team, fostering strong internal and cross-functional collaboration. Ensure their productivity, development, and overall performance align with Co-Impact goals. Monitor employee morale and implement initiatives to address concerns and improve the workplace. Collaborate with Human Resources to attract, recruit, onboard, mentor, and develop talent in the region.
  • As a member of the Co-Impact Leadership Team, actively engage in shaping management decisions regarding the growth, strategy and priorities of Co-Impact and provide strategic guidance to the CEO and as part of the Leadership Team on initiatives and opportunities.
  • Serve as a key leader in developing and modelling a personal and team culture that embodies Co-Impact values. Foster an outcomes-focused approach to achieve meaningful, lasting, and inclusive impact, prioritize program partners, maintain a beginner’s mind; leverage unity in diversity and build trusting partnerships.

Qualifications and Experience

  • At least 15 years of professional experience and with deep expertise in advancing gender equality through an intersectional lens, and substantial knowledge in at least one of our sectoral focus areas (education, health, and economic opportunity).
  • Extensive experience as an outcomes-focused, program partner-centered grant-maker, with a proven track record of supporting civil society initiatives in the Global South with a particular focus on Asia.
  • Extensive experience of living and working in and understanding the political economies of the Global South with a particular focus on Asia.
  • At least 5 years of experience managing a team and mentoring staff to achieve strong results while fostering a positive work culture.
  • A university degree or equivalent in a relevant area (Masters’ degree preferred).
  • Fluency in English is required.

Required Skills

  • Strategic Agility: Ability to identify high-potential opportunities and the design of strategic approaches backed by evidence-based analysis.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Demonstrated experience building and managing relationships with senior government and other external stakeholders, with sound judgment in navigating complex political, policy and regulatory environments.
  • Organizational Effectiveness: Proven track record of delivering results through strategic coherence, thoughtful business strategy, strong leadership, and a solid understanding of operations.
  • Decision Making: Skillful in considering diverse perspectives, and making good judgements based on values and principles, data, experience, and risk assessment.
  • Working with People: Experience in motivating, contributing to, and managing collaborative teams to achieve shared goals productively, effectively, and inclusively.
  • Managing Action with Purpose and Values: Ability to inspire colleagues and drive initiatives in alignment with the organization’s core purpose and values.
  • Results-orientation: Strong project management skills, including deadline management, a sense of responsibility and accountability, the ability to handle multiple tasks and responsibilities, and work effectively remotely.
  • Interpersonal Savvy: Proficient in making and nurturing relationships both inside and outside the organization, with a keen appreciation of intercultural dynamics, and an inclusive style. Comfortable engaging with senior leaders and representing Co-Impact effectively.
  • Dealing with Ambiguity: Capable of navigating uncertainty and risk with ease, making decisions and acting even without a complete picture.
  • Learning Orientation: Intellectually curious, seeking evidence, openness to new ideas and diverse perspectives, and willing to admit and learn from failure.
  • Strong Moral Compass: Upholds impeccable personal ethics and integrity, demonstrating kindness and care.
  • Communications: excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to effectively manage and influence a diverse range of relationships in a multicultural environment.
  • Global Flexibility: Ability to adapt to working across different time zones and be flexible with working hours and international travel. Proven effectiveness in collaborating with remote and diverse teams.
  • Collaborative Focus: Demonstrates strong and infectious enthusiasm for collaboration and partnership and recognizes the value in fostering an environment that supports shared communications, efforts and results.
  • Writing Ability: Ability to write and communicate ideas with clarity and precision.
  • Perspective: Maintains a sense of humor and ability to not take oneself too seriously.
  • Financial understanding: Basic knowledge of organizational financial models, financial statements, strategic financial analysis/ projections, and budgeting.
  • Feminist Principles: Commitment to feminist core principles including power-sharing power, dismantling biases, promoting diversity, fostering self-awareness, practicing collective care, upholding accountability, encouraging collaboration, and demonstrating courage.

Benefits

Co-Impact’s compensation philosophy is guided by the following three principles:

  • Equity and Fairness: Our approach to compensation and benefits are designed to ensure that our global team is treated equitably regardless of location and without regard to gender, race, or nationality.
  • Transparency: We want Co-Impact’s employees to understand our salary structure and to feel confident that they are paid equitably, and potential job applicants to have an understanding of how the role for which they are applying will be compensated.
  • Accountability: As stewards of the philanthropic resources entrusted to us so that we can support our program partners, we are accountable to our donors and our board, to our staff, and to the general public.

In accordance with that philosophy, we include the salary for each position in our job postings. To ensure equity within the organization and for all candidates, we do not negotiate salary or benefits. The role is remote and flexible for candidates who are authorized to live and work in India. As we work across multiple regions, candidates should be comfortable collaborating across time zones, including having late‑afternoon meetings. The annual gross salary is USD200,000 (paid in INR based on FX rate determined at the point of offer) plus a generous benefits package.

Application Details

You are welcome to express your interest by submitting a tailored CV and cover letter that speak directly to this role and highlight your relevant experience. Applications that are generic, non-specific, or clearly AI-generated will be less competitive.

Please apply online by 5:00 PM India Standard Time (GMT+5:30) on 19 August 2026. In your cover letter, please confirm that you are authorized to live and work in one of the locations listed above. Please note that Co‑Impact cannot cover relocation costs.

Thank you for your understanding. We will review applications on a rolling basis. The position may close early if we receive a strong pool of candidates, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Role Title: NDT Subject Matter Expert – Laser Shearography (Level II / Level III)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging NDT Subject Matter Experts – Laser Shearography (Level II / Level III) to support a customer's advanced aerospace inspection project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Conduct rigorous manual analysis of laser shearography data, including fringe patterns and interferograms, to identify and characterize composite material defects.
  2. Review and interpret technical case papers, test logs, and inspection limits for aerospace applications using NDT standards.
  3. Evaluate and document defect types, severity, and potential impact on composite structures, providing detailed rationale for decisions.
  4. Deliver comprehensive written feedback on inspection findings, supporting the development and refinement of technical protocols.
  5. Collaborate remotely with project managers and technical stakeholders via clear, professional written and verbal communication.
  6. Ensure that all assessments and reviews are completed without the aid of AI tools, maintaining the highest standard of manual inspection integrity.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current ASNT / NAS 410 / ISO 9712 Level II or Level III certification in Laser Shearography or related NDT methods.
  2. Extensive hands-on experience with laser shearography, particularly in aerospace or advanced composite inspection scenarios.
  3. Demonstrated expertise interpreting shearography fringe patterns and optical interferometry data for defect evaluation.
  4. Strong analytical skills in defect identification, root cause analysis, and reporting within stringent aerospace standards.
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities, including technical documentation and collaborative problem-solving.
  6. Familiarity with industry best practices for non-destructive inspection of composite materials.
  7. Experience providing technical guidance or quality engineering for similar NDT projects – direct inspection or review background is highly valued.

Dudek’s journey began in 1980 with a vision to serve Southern California’s water and wastewater agencies.

Today, we are a 100% employee-owned firm supporting clients nationwide and delivering projects that improve and protect the built and natural environments of communities throughout the United States. Our work has been recognized by leading industry organizations, and we’ve been honored with multiple national Top Workplace Awards.

Our employee-owners are unified by a singular commitment to supporting projects that address key societal issues, such as the transition to renewable energy, infrastructure hardening and repair, environmental protection, and community resilience.

Learn more about our award-winning culture, the benefits and perks of being a Dudekian, and the projects you will have the opportunity to shape.

Position Overview

Who You Are

As an employee-owner, you embrace accountability, working safely, and collaboration while thinking resourcefully and independently.

Like all Dudekians, you are curious and solution-oriented, with the ability to adapt quickly to changes and approach challenges with a spirit of innovation.

How You’ll Make an Impact

Dudek is currently seeking a full-time senior-level Cultural Resources/Architectural Historian Senior Project Manager to help lead and expand our cultural resources services in the Southeast. The successful candidate will work in close partnership with our Southeast Lead Archaeologist, pairing built environment, regulatory, and project leadership experience with archaeological expertise. This position will oversee a full range of cultural resources services, lead business development, prepare scopes and cost estimates, serve as a senior technical expert, and build relationships with clients, agencies, State Historic Preservation Offices (SHPOs), and consulting parties. This role will also help guide projects through Section 106, Section 4(f), NEPA, and applicable state review processes and mentor early- and mid-career staff as the Southeast practice grows.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partner with Dudek’s Southeast Lead Archaeologist to build and grow the cultural resources practice, combining built environment and archaeology services into an integrated offering;
  • Develop a shared growth strategy with the Southeast Lead Archaeologist, including target clients, agencies, markets, and contract vehicles, and track progress against that strategy;
  • Jointly pursue and deliver projects, sharing technical leadership so archaeology and built environment work move together through survey, evaluation, effects assessment, and mitigation;
  • Coordinate with Dudek planners, environmental staff, and cultural resources groups in other regions to incorporate Southeast cultural resources services into larger pursuits;
  • Lead projects through Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, including 36 CFR Part 800, Section 4(f), NEPA, and applicable state review laws, from identification and evaluation through resolution of adverse effects;
  • Assess effects on historic properties and prepare Finding of Effect documentation for federal and state agencies;
  • Lead consultation with SHPOs, federal agencies, Tribes, local governments, and consulting parties and build consensus among interested and affected parties;
  • Negotiate and author Memoranda of Agreement and Programmatic Agreements;
  • Develop creative mitigation measures, including HABS/HAER/HALS documentation, historic context studies, NRHP nominations, interpretive markers and displays, and public outreach;
  • Advise clients and project teams on regulatory strategies for complex, multi-year projects;
  • Oversee cultural resources surveys, from reconnaissance-level surveys through intensive-level documentation;
  • Oversee the evaluation of historic-era properties under NRHP, state register, and local designation criteria;
  • Provide oversight for complex resource types, including historic bridges, roadways, canals, railroads, historic districts, and mid-twentieth-century development;
  • Apply the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties in federal, state, and local regulatory settings;
  • Work with state site files and SHPO inventory systems across the Southeast, including the Florida Master Site File, Georgia’s GNAHRGIS, and South Carolina’s ArchSite;
  • Contribute to policies, guidance, and best practices for identifying and evaluating historic resources;
  • Present findings and documentation at agency meetings, public meetings, and historic preservation board meetings;
  • Lead research and writing for historic context statements and registration requirements and oversee property-specific research;
  • Prepare and oversee survey and evaluation reports, effects assessments, and cultural resources sections for NEPA documents, including Environmental Assessments and Environmental Impact Statements;
  • Provide senior-level review of internal and external work products and establish and maintain best practices for documentation, report templates, and data management;
  • Mentor early- and mid-career staff on project and proposal efforts, delegate technical work, provide guidance on technical approaches, and develop internal training;
  • Work with the Southeast Lead Archaeologist to identify staffing needs and recruit as the Southeast practice grows;
  • Assume formal staff-supervision responsibilities as the Southeast team grows;
  • Build long-term relationships with agency, municipal, and private clients and act as a seller-doer who turns existing work into new opportunities and cross-sells services with other Dudek teams;
  • Lead business development for cultural resources and built environment work in the Southeast, including relationships with clients, agencies, and SHPOs;
  • Prepare scopes of work, cost estimates, and proposal content based on project and regulatory needs;
  • Manage projects and deliverables from initiation through completion and ensure deadlines are met;
  • Manage budgets, schedules, client invoicing, project status, and staff billing, with support from other project managers as needed;
  • Communicate regularly with internal project managers and clients.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in history, architectural history, historic preservation, or a related field;
  • 20+ years of professional experience in federal permitting, cultural resources management, architectural history, or historic preservation regulatory compliance;
  • Meets the Secretary of the Interior’s Professional Qualification Standards for Architectural History;
  • Ability to travel as needed;
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license and have active personal automobile liability insurance by the first day of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 25+ years of professional experience in cultural resources management, architectural history, and federal permitting in the Southeastern United States;
  • Experience working with multiple Southeastern SHPOs and their survey and reporting guidelines;
  • Experience with transportation, energy, or federal agency projects, such as FHWA/state DOT, USACE, or FERC projects;
  • Previous staff management experience;
  • Experience preparing NRHP nominations, Multiple Property Documentation Forms, or historic context studies;
  • Proficiency with GIS and mobile data collection tools;
  • Excellent technical writing and research skills, with experience providing senior-level review;
  • Experience coordinating with multidisciplinary teams, including archaeologists, planners, and environmental staff.

Compensation: $135,000-155,000/annually*

*Final agreed-upon compensation will be based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, an individual’s related experience, education, certifications, skills, and work location. Successful candidates must pass a pre-employment drug test and background check prior to beginning employment.

Working Conditions

  • This job operates in a remote or office-based environment and this role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, printers, etc.
  • This job requires occasional project site visits, based outdoors which can include excessive noise, uneven walking surfaces, extreme weather, and moving vehicles and equipment.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. This job requires the following:

  • Working on a computer, sitting, or standing for long periods of time in an office or remote office setting.
  • Attending meetings, both in person and virtually, and speaking on the phone with peers, clients, etc.
  • Specific vision abilities, including close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

They sell into organizations where privacy, cybersecurity, executive protection, legal risk, and employee safety matter. This includes law firms, corporate security teams, executive-protection firms, cyber-insurance providers, benefits brokers, PEOs, and enterprise organizations.

This is a Founding Account Executive role and the company's first dedicated revenue hire.

This is not a role where you inherit a large sales team, SDR team, or marketing engine. This is for a proven seller who can self-source pipeline, open doors, run complex sales cycles, and close revenue.

The company already has a working product, real enterprise revenue, channel opportunities, and buyers who understand the problem. Now they need the first true sales producer who can bring the market in.

If you are a proven closer who knows how to open doors, build pipeline, and close complex B2B deals, this could be a strong fit.

Deine Mission:

Du wirst zur fachlichen Stimme unseres Sales und Account Management Teams.

Unsere Account Executives & Account Manager führen die kommerziellen Gespräche. Du bringst die Security-Expertise ein, mit der aus interessierten Unternehmen überzeugte Kunden werden.

  • Lösungen gestalten:Du definierst gemeinsam mit dem Sales-Team den richtigen Projektumfang und überzeugst Kunden mit nachvollziehbaren Empfehlungen.

  • Den Vertrieb weiterentwickeln:Als erste Person in dieser Rolle entwickelst du Best Practices, Demo-Konzepte und Prozesse, die langfristig skalieren.

  • Unser Produkt mitgestalten:Du bringst Kundenfeedback direkt zu unserem Produkt-Team und beeinflusst damit die Weiterentwicklung unserer Plattform.

Kurz gesagt:Du verbindest Security-Know-how mit Beratung, Produkt und Business Impact – ohne selbst klassische Kaltakquise betreiben zu müssen.

Deine Erfahrung:

Das ist uns wichtig:

  • Du hast praktische Erfahrung mit ISO 27001 und Informationssicherheitsmanagement (ISMS) – zum Beispiel aus der Beratung, Implementierung oder einer internen Security-Rolle.

  • Kenntnisse zu NIS2, TISAX oder weiteren Compliance-Frameworks

  • Erfahrung mit Demos, Scoping oder technischen Verkaufsprozessen

  • ISO-27001-Zertifizierungen

Kein Problem. Wenn du Lust hast, näher am Produkt, an Kundenentscheidungen und am Business zu arbeiten, möchten wir dich kennenlernen.

Du musst nicht jede Anforderung zu 100 % erfüllen.

jobs.description:
National Sales Executive – Freight Brokerage

Location: Remote – United States
Preference: Middle Tennessee / reasonable proximity to company headquarters preferred, but exceptional candidates nationwide will be considered
Employment Type: Full-Time, W-2
Openings: 1–2

Build the Business. Own the Hunt. Get Rewarded.

An established, family-owned transportation and logistics company is looking for an experienced National Sales Executive – Freight Brokerage to help lead the next phase of growth.

This is a true hunter sales role. We're looking for someone who wakes up thinking, Who can I sell today?

Your primary responsibility will be to identify and win new shipper relationships, develop freight opportunities, and bring new business into the organization. Once the business is won, you'll have an experienced brokerage and operations team behind you to help execute it.

You sell. We execute.

This is an opportunity for an accomplished logistics salesperson to make a meaningful impact at an established, financially healthy company that is actively building its next generation of sales leadership.

About the Company

Our client is an established, family-owned transportation and logistics company approaching its 25th anniversary.

With approximately 20 employees, the company has built a strong reputation through organic growth and a long-tenured team. Many employees have been with the organization for a decade or longer.

The company's historical foundation includes printed media distribution and LTL transportation, which remains an important and profitable part of the business. However, leadership is strategically expanding its freight brokerage operation, particularly truckload and broader transportation services.

The infrastructure is already in place. Now the company is investing in the sales talent needed to accelerate growth.

The Opportunity

As National Sales Executive, you'll be responsible for:

  • Hunting for and winning new shipper accounts
  • Prospecting through cold calling, email, networking, referrals, and other outbound strategies
  • Building relationships with transportation decision-makers
  • Identifying freight opportunities and developing a qualified pipeline
  • Personally leading the sales process from prospecting through close
  • Growing revenue and margin through new customer acquisition
  • Selling truckload, LTL, and other transportation solutions based on customer needs
  • Developing opportunities across a variety of commodities and freight types
  • Meeting with customers virtually and in person when appropriate
  • Working closely with leadership and operations to successfully onboard new business
  • Transitioning day-to-day freight execution to the existing operations team so you can remain focused on business development
  • Maintaining consistent activity, pipeline development, customer meetings, and revenue-producing efforts

This is not a cradle-to-grave brokerage position where you'll spend your days finding customers and your nights covering trucks.

Your job is to find the freight and grow the business.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Proven sales experience within freight brokerage, logistics, transportation, or a closely related industry
  • Demonstrated history of hunting and winning new shipper business
  • Strong prospecting and cold-calling skills
  • Ability to independently develop a sales pipeline
  • Strong understanding of the transportation industry
  • Demonstrated sales production and measurable results
  • Excellent relationship-building and communication skills
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment
  • Entrepreneurial mindset and strong sense of ownership
  • Comfort being measured on activity, pipeline development, revenue, and margin production

Strongly Preferred

  • Existing relationships with shippers or transportation decision-makers
  • Demonstrated ability to build a book of business from scratch
  • Specific examples of significant accounts personally won
  • History of producing measurable revenue and/or gross margin
  • Experience selling multiple transportation modes or services
  • Strong customer-facing presentation skills
  • Experience with truckload, LTL, reefer, flatbed, oversized, specialized, or other brokerage services
  • Experience selling customized or comprehensive transportation solutions

Your Existing Book Is Welcome — But It's Not Required

We value candidates with strong existing relationships, but you do not need to bring a portable book of business to be successful here.

If you're currently subject to a non-solicit or other restriction that prevents you from approaching existing customers, we will still consider you.

What matters most is whether you've demonstrated that you can consistently win business.

If you've built a book once, we believe you can build another one.

Why Join This Opportunity?

Sell Without Getting Buried in Operations

You'll have an experienced team supporting the freight after you bring it in.

The existing infrastructure includes:

  • Brokerage management
  • Experienced brokerage and operations professionals
  • Pricing support
  • LTL pricing expertise
  • IT support
  • Accounting
  • AP/AR
  • Carrier payment support
  • Invoicing
  • Tracking
  • Claims support
  • Established TMS and technology infrastructure

You won't be expected to do everything yourself.

Uncapped Earning Potential

We want producers to make money.

The compensation structure includes a competitive base salary and uncapped commission, with earning potential tied directly to production.

Compensation is flexible based on experience, demonstrated production, and overall fit.

Join an Established Company That's Still Building

The company has nearly 25 years of history, a financially healthy business, and an experienced team — but is still small enough that one great salesperson can make a significant difference.

You're not stepping into a finished sales organization.

You're helping build the next one.

Potential for Growth

The company is intentionally expanding its sales organization, and successful early hires can have opportunities to take on greater responsibility and leadership as the organization grows.

The company prefers to promote from within.

Instead of simply climbing the corporate ladder, you'll have an opportunity to help build the ladder.

Family-Owned Culture

You'll work directly with leadership in an organization where relationships matter.

This is not a giant brokerage where you're simply another number. The company values long-term employees, personal accountability, collaboration, and the ability to make things happen without layers of corporate bureaucracy.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive base salary based on experience and proven production
  • Uncapped commission
  • Health insurance
  • Company-provided laptop/workstation
  • Business travel support
  • Company credit card may be provided after an initial period
  • Support for customer visits and face-to-face selling
  • Travel expenses supported when there is a legitimate business case
  • Strong operational support behind every new customer you win

The philosophy is simple:

If the activity generates business and makes money, we'll support it.

What Success Looks Like

We understand that strong relationships don't always turn into immediate revenue.

During the initial 60–90 days, we'll be looking for evidence that you're building toward success:

  • Consistent prospecting activity
  • Meaningful conversations with shippers
  • Customer meetings
  • Qualified opportunities entering the pipeline
  • Reactivation of relevant relationships
  • Growing pipeline value
  • Forward momentum toward revenue and margin

We're willing to provide a reasonable runway to build the business.

What we don't want is someone who spends months collecting a paycheck without creating meaningful activity or opportunity.

Who Will Thrive Here?

This role is ideal for someone who:

  • Loves hunting for new business
  • Gets energized by opening doors
  • Has a proven history of winning freight
  • Wants significant earning potential
  • Doesn't need to be micromanaged
  • Wants the freedom of a remote sales environment
  • Values having a strong operations team behind them
  • Enjoys working with ownership and leadership directly
  • Wants to help build something rather than simply inherit a territory
  • Sees an opportunity where others see a small company

If your favorite part of logistics is winning the customer, we'd like to talk.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move quickly:

1. Video Interview

Initial conversation via Teams.

2. Leadership Interview
Additional discussion with business development leadership and company leadership.

For select, highly compensated candidates, a final onsite meeting may be requested.

We're prepared to move quickly for the right producer.

The MarTechProduct Manager – AEP serves as the strategic and technical owner of Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) within the MarTech ecosystem. This role will lead the end-to-end management of AEP, including schema planning, audience segmentation, data readiness, personalization enablement, and international sandbox rollout. With a focus on scalability, governance, and business alignment, this role ensures AEP is configured to support high-impact customer engagement use cases across the organization, international markets, as well as across partners.

ResponsibilitiesKey Role and Responsibilities:

  • Own the Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) roadmap, backlog, and delivery cycles across the organization, international markets, and partners.
  • Lead schema planning and evolution in collaboration with Data & Analytics and downstream marketing activation teams.
  • Define and manage scalable segment strategies to support personalization, measurement, and campaign activation.
  • Ensure effective enablement and rollout of international AEP sandboxes and localization support for schema and segmentation.
  • Partner with Marketing Ops, Customer Journey teams, and partners to translate business requirements into platform use cases.
  • Collaborate with AJO and CJA product managers to ensure audience readiness and platform alignment across the stack.
  • Work with Data Engineering to ensure proper data ingestion, data quality, and identity stitching within AEP.
  • Define governance models for segment naming, consent tracking, and sandbox management.
  • Facilitate user feedback loops, and documentation for both business and technical stakeholders.
  • Monitor platform performance, usage metrics, and help drive adoption across business units and international markets.

QualificationsRequirements:

  • 7+ years of experience in product management, MarTech, or data platforms.
  • 3+ years working directly with Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) or equivalent CDP.
  • Experience managing platform roadmaps, requirements intake, and backlog grooming.
  • Strong understanding of customer segmentation, personalization, and activation workflows.
  • Proven experience launching global or multi-regional marketing technology platforms.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with both technical and business stakeholders.
  • Bachelors degree in marketing, business, technology, or a related field

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience with AEP schema design and segment building.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Journey Optimizer (AJO) and Customer Journey Analytics (CJA).
  • Understanding of data privacy and consent management frameworks.
  • Experience working in a federated or matrixed enterprise environment.
  • Adobe certifications in AEP, AJO, or related technologies are a plus.

jobs.excerpt: Eaton’s Electrical division is currently seeking a Lead Design Engineer - Structural Steel.
jobs.description:
Eaton’s Electrical division is currently seeking a Lead Design Engineer - Structural Steel. The position is remote, with anticipated travel of up to 10%.

Eaton's Data Center Solutions division is seeking a Lead Design Engineer - Structural Steel with proven expertise in tubular steel structure design, analysis, and documentation for data center whitespace infrastructure. This is a specialist-level individual contributor role who bring independent analytical rigor, code-level structural calculation fluency, and direct experience designing the structural systems that support overhead power, cooling, containment, and cable management infrastructure within live and new-build data center environments.

The expected annual salary range for this role is $97,000 - $143,000 a year.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

What we offer:

Eaton's Data Center Solutions division is at the center of one of the most capital-intensive infrastructure build cycles in history — powering and cooling the compute that runs AI, cloud, and enterprise applications worldwide. This Engineering Specialist role offers a structural engineer with a consulting background the opportunity to apply deep technical expertise inside a product and manufacturing organization: influencing how structural systems are designed, standardized, and scaled across thousands of data center deployments.

Eaton provides a comprehensive benefits package including competitive base salary, annual performance incentive bonus, medical/dental/vision, 401(k) with company match, paid time off, tuition reimbursement, and access to Eaton's learning and development platforms.

What you’ll do:

  • Design and analyze structural systems for data center whitespace infrastructure, including power distribution, containment systems, cable management, cooling equipment supports, and modular assemblies.
  • Perform structural engineering calculations, member sizing, connection design, and load analysis for gravity, seismic, lateral, and dynamic loading conditions.
  • Develop complete structural calculation packages, including load assessments, deflection checks, anchorage design, and supporting documentation for design reviews and approvals.
  • Evaluate complex assemblies using structural analysis tools (e.g., SAP2000, FEA software) and validate results with engineering judgment and hand calculations.
  • Assess and modify existing infrastructure for retrofit, upgrade, and capacity expansion projects, ensuring structures can safely support new loads.
  • Create and coordinate structural drawings and BIM/Revit models, including fabrication details, installation plans, clash detection, and multi-discipline coordination.
  • Support new product development by collaborating with mechanical and MEP teams, providing structural input, risk assessments, design-for-manufacturing feedback, and testing requirements.
  • Serve as the structural engineering expert for customers, contractors, engineers of record, and regulators, supporting delegated design submittals, technical reviews, project proposals, and site-specific solutions.

This role could be the next step in your career if you demonstrate the following experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Civil, or Structural Engineering from an accredited institution
  • Minimum of five (5) years of structural engineering or engineering mechanics experience.

You will set yourself apart by demonstrating some or all of the following:

  • Master's degree in Structural Engineering with thesis or research focus in steel structures, connection design, or structural dynamics.
  • PE (Professional Engineer) licensure preferred
  • Direct experience designing overhead whitespace infrastructure for data centers: containment frames, busway and cable tray support structures, cooling pipe support systems, and related non-building structural assemblies.
  • Familiarity with AISC Design Guide series relevant to HSS connections, torsion, and welded steel construction.

Position Success Criteria:

  • Strong background in structural analysis, structural dynamics, structural design, and engineering mechanics for with structural systems in data center, mission-critical, industrial, or manufacturing facility environments — specifically overhead support structures, non-building structures, or equipment support platforms is required.
  • Proficiency in structural analysis software: SAP2000, LS-DYNA, or equivalent frame/FEA tools; ability to validate software output with hand calculations.
  • Working knowledge of Autodesk Revit for structural modeling and Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) for multi-discipline coordination.

    • Minimum 3 years of clinical experience with psychiatric populations.

    • Minimum 3 years administering scales in clinical research trials (excluding graduate/doctoral research).

  • Skills:

    • Strong interpersonal and communication skills for professional interaction at all levels.

    • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, time management, and problem-solving ability.

    • Proficiency with Windows and Microsoft Office applications.

Current openings require fluency in English and native-level proficiency in Italian.

JOB OVERVIEW:

ITC Federal is seeking a detail-oriented Contracts Administrator who will support the drafting, review, negotiation, and administration of contracts within ITC Federal. This role helps ensure that contracts align with legal requirements and organizational objectives while identifying potential risks, monitoring contract performance, maintaining records, and collaborating with various departments to facilitate successful and compliant business relationships.

Responsibilities

  • Provide proposal support to include the review of terms/conditions, completion of representations/certifications, and performance of compliance reviews.
  • Support the negotiation of contracts, subcontracts, and other agreements with prime contractors, vendors, and subcontractors under the guidance of senior contracts staff.
  • Support ad hoc projects, data tracking, reporting, and other due diligence requests.
  • Issue subcontract request for proposals in support of proposal efforts.
  • Support proposal preparation, submissions, response to Requests for Proposals/Quotes
  • Review contract awards and modifications for accuracy.
  • Draft and issue subcontract modifications reflective of prime contract requirements and in accordance with operations’ requests.
  • Identify and recommend opportunities to streamline contracts processes.
  • Coordinate with operations and finance to implement contract set up in Costpoint accounting system.
  • Confirm and track insurance needs and request insurance certificates.
  • Maintain and track internal contractual reporting deadlines.
  • Redline corporate documents and contracts, escalating non-standard terms to senior contracts staff as needed.
  • Participate in and contribute to process improvement activities.
  • Apply working knowledge of government contracting principles to day-to-day contracting matters.
  • Maintain centralized filing of all contractual documents.
  • Manage contracts actions as they are routed through internal departments for approval.
  • Input contract information into the contracts repository in a timely manner.

Qualifications
